reference.question: Calculate: \(\frac{4}{5} \div 2 = ?\)
reference.solution:
Method 1: Multiply by the reciprocal

\(\frac{4}{5} \div 2 = \frac{4}{5} \times \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{5}\).

Method 2: Share fifths equally

Keep \(\frac{1}{5}\) as the unit: \(\frac{4}{5}\) contains four of these units. Two equal shares contain \(4\div2=2\) units each, so \(\frac{4}{5}\div2=\frac{2}{5}\).

edges.reason: The target explicitly includes the multiplication-division relation, so multiplication meaning is needed for that inverse-operation assertion.
The stated method finds quotients using two-through-six multiplication facts, requiring the corresponding product values.
Both fair-sharing and number-of-groups questions use division's meanings rather than merely a numerical table lookup.
A general fraction takes several equal unit parts; one such part is the unit-fraction concept directly contained in that construction.
edges.scope: fraction as a count of unit fractional parts

edges.reason: The criteria expressly find common factors and reduce until numerator and denominator are coprime. These are the common-factor contents of the endpoint; finding the greatest factor in a single step is only a shortcut and is outside this required scope.
edges.scope: Finding a shared divisor and recognizing the absence of a shared divisor above one when reducing to simplest form

edges.reason: Reduction replaces numerator and denominator by division by the same common factor, using the value-preserving fraction property.
edges.scope: dividing numerator and denominator by a common number

edges.reason: The integer-multiplier case supplies a useful stepping stone and repeated-addition interpretation. The product-of-numerators/product-of-denominators rule follows directly from a part-of-a-part area model without executing the earlier decimal-free integer-multiplier procedure; Gemini confuses this customary progression with necessity.
The source explicitly changes division by an integer into multiplication by its fractional reciprocal, then computes that fraction product.
edges.scope: multiplying by the reciprocal of the integer
